fields.asset_name: Umicore Loyalist (eastern Ontario) CAM and pCAM plant
fields.product: NMC cathode active material (with integrated pCAM)

rows.notes: Loveland/Loyalist (Loyalist Township, Ontario). Construction paused July 2024; plant had been expected to begin production in 2026 (S6); output stated as CAM for 800,000 EVs/yr (S5), no tonnage. Umicore announced 'CAM and pCAM plant in Ontario, Canada' in Oct 2023 (S21). Whether the project was later cancelled is not confirmed in sources opened (a 2025 strategic update, not opened, may have changed it). Status under_construction taken from 'pause on the construction' wording; ground-breaking date not verified. Original announcement year 2022 per S5 text ('Initially announced in 2022', page extraction).

Umicore (Belgium HQ) CAM capacity in Korea planned to reach 40 GWh after remaining capex (S3; page extraction: 'bring CAM capacity in Poland to 45 GWh and Korea to 40 GWh'). Site not named in sources opened (Cheonan is believed but NOT confirmed). Overlaps SC012 (Korea); lead to dedupe. Quote in S3 is the extractor's rendering; verify. GWh only, capacity null.

BASF Factbook lists 'CAM manufacturing plant in Schwarzheide, Germany' (2023 entry); BASF said in Apr 2024 Schwarzheide operations are not affected by the Harjavalta delay (S7, extractor rendering); 2020 plan was start-up in 2022 (S8). Capacity: only 'initial capacities ... around 400,000 full electric vehicles per year' for the new plants jointly (2020), no tonnage. Start year not verified; status operational is inferred from S7/S9 phrasing, not from an explicit 'commercial production' statement.

Precursor (not CAM) row, added because it was on SC013 list; precursor-task owner should dedupe by id. Plant built (construction started 2020, S8) but formal start-up blocked: April 2024 BASF started change negotiations, 'further postponement of and uncertainty around the formal startup date' (S7). Vaasa Administrative Court cancelled a temporary permit in Feb 2024 (electrive 2024-04-12, opened, not cited as a source here). A June-2024 report (search summary only) says BASF abandoned the plans: not confirmed; status after 2024 unverified. No capacity figure found.

Current ownership/operational status NOT re-confirmed (source is 2018). jv_partners wording is loose; BASF Toda America was a BASF/TODA JV in 2018.

2018 release (S10) names Battle Creek as a BTA CAM facility. A BASF 2024 site fact sheet (found via search, fetch returned 403) reportedly describes Battle Creek as producing cathode materials with 50 employees (year-end 2023 data) - not cited (not opened). No capacity figure found.

BSBM combined target is 100 kt/yr CAM across Changsha (Hunan) and Shuizuishan (Ningxia) after the 2022 expansion ('BSBM to achieve 100 kt annual capacity', S11) - no per-site split found, so capacity null on both rows; do NOT sum both rows with 100 kt. BASF Factbook lists a 2023 'CAM capacity expansion for the joint venture BASF Shanshan in Chansha' (S9). JV share 51/49 is reported-tier (S12). Possible overlap with SC009-011 (Shanshan's own ids) - lead to dedupe.

See Changsha row for the combined 100 kt figure. Source says BSBM 'is expanding' capacity here (2022); whether this site is solely CAM vs pCAM was not stated in the quote. Current status not re-confirmed after 2022.

CAM portion of Apex 1 was dropped in March 2025 when Ascend and DOE agreed to cancel the $164M CAM grant (S14 title, reported tier; Canary Media S13 says Apex 1 'is still happening' as pCAM/lithium carbonate). Canary article (opened) reports Ascend 'scrapping plans' for CAM; wording not quoted verbatim. No CAM tonnage found.

Precursor row added for completeness (precursor-task owner to dedupe). Canary 2025-03-05: completion target moved to Q3 2026 and Apex 1 'still happening' (S13). Search summaries (not opened) say construction paused since late 2024. A Texas bankruptcy court approved a $31.7M bid by Turner-Kokosing JV for the facility on 'June 4' (S15; year not shown in extracted text - likely 2026, unverified), i.e. the site changed hands via Chapter 11; current project state uncertain. Paused state is an inference.

Only evidence is the title of a Renewables Now 2024 article cited by Wikipedia: 'Northvolt ditches plan for CAM giga-factory in Sweden, sells land' (S16). Town (Skellefteå) NOT confirmed in sources opened; no capacity or announcement date found. Northvolt AB applied for bankruptcy in Sweden 2025-03-12 (Wikipedia extract). Original article not opened.
